application:account-linking:federated-em.decision: A federated sign-in joins an existing account only when the provider says the email is verified (email_verified is True); otherwise it creates a separate account, and an unverified email never takes ownership of an address

database:primary-key:user.decision: One User entity with opaque string ids (random uuid4 hex) for every account; A's integer ids and B's 'lu-<n>' ids kept in legacy_id if data is ever imported

database:field-type:user.id.decision: User.id is text (uuid4 hex) for all accounts; integer A ids widen to text in legacy_id

application:auth-provider:provider.decision: One identity system: local password provider plus external OAuth providers, all resolving to one User through an Identity table keyed by (provider, subject)

application:authorization-model:model.decision: C's RBAC (role -> permission set) is the one authorization model; A's and B's unchecked role strings are mapped into it

application:business-rule:default_role.decision: Password registration gets editor (A user -> editor); new OAuth accounts get viewer (B member -> viewer); a joined account keeps its existing role

application:roles:roles.decision: Unified roles viewer, editor, admin; mapping A user -> editor, B member -> viewer, C roles unchanged; any other source role raises KeyError

application:business-rule:duplicate-regi.decision: Reject a duplicate email (case-insensitive) with an error instead of overwriting the account

application:permissions:role-change-acto.decision: set_role resolves the caller from the session token; only admins (manage_roles) may change roles; the role must be viewer/editor/admin; nobody can raise their own role
application:permissions:role-change-acto.note: admin-only and no self-raise are user decisions in task.md; actor-from-session and role validation pre-approved by the benchmark operator

application:auth-methods:methods.decision: Offer both password and OAuth sign-in through the one identity system

database:duplicate-entity:user.decision: Merge A:User and B:Account into one User entity; B's provider and subject move to an Identity entity linked to User

migration:user.decision: Plan approved: re-key to uuid ids with legacy_id. Both sources keep data only in process memory, so there is no persisted data to migrate in this run; running any real migration needs its own approval
